overall_summary: Deduplicated performance analysis indicates that space exploration, planetary anomalies, and extreme 'What If' scenarios are significantly outperforming other niches in both views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view). Specifically, videos focusing on extreme worlds (e.g., diamond planets, extreme weather, and dark planets published within the last 30 days) generate the highest sustained velocity. Conversely, standard biological facts and psychological tricks show lower momentum in recent sample windows.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) achieved over 1,000 views rapidly, with high like ratios compared to older psychological or standard biology shorts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-concept cosmic 'What If' scenarios and bizarre planetary extremes using vivid, high-contrast visual descriptions.

winning_patterns.pattern: High-Stakes Curiosity Hooks ('Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year')
winning_patterns.evidence: A9Qa-RmuOr0 secured 980 views and 21 likes by contrasting counter-intuitive planetary mechanics directly in the title.
winning_patterns.action: Use time-scale or scale-comparison paradoxes in titles to trigger instant cognitive dissonance.

weak_patterns.evidence: Older octopus and memory-related shorts (e.g., AXAfwrzzEdU, 5AN7LUgqarc) stalled out with lower engagement relative to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Pause standard animal fact repetitions and pivot toward high-production cinematic animal survival or fresh, less-explored ecological mysteries.

weak_patterns.pattern: Static Psychological Triggers Without High-Concept Visuals
weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts addressing songs stuck in the head (ef3ND4qiRHc) generated lower daily view velocity than planetary concepts.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard psychological life-hacks unless framed as extreme, high-tension micro-mysteries.
